editorial:
Imagine you are stepping back into old Edo Japan where every corner holds a secret. You get to follow Heiji, a clever investigator who finds a dead body at a shrine with a strange blueprint in his pocket. It feels like a classic detective story, but it has a lot of heart. While Heiji tries to figure out if there is a big government cover-up, he meets Tsubame, a traveling performer who is amazing on stage but very sad inside. The chemistry between them adds a nice emotional layer to the mystery, making you care about the people as much as the crime.

The acting is top-notch, and the way the mystery unfolds keeps you guessing without being too confusing. Some parts move a bit slow when they focus on the romance, but the payoff at the end is totally worth it. If you like historical dramas with a good puzzle, you will love this.
endingExplained: It turns out the blueprint was a map to a hidden vault used by corrupt officials to hide stolen taxes. Tsubame was actually the daughter of a man framed by these officials years ago. Heiji helps her get revenge by exposing the villains in a public trial. The movie ends with the bad guys going to jail and Heiji and Tsubame sharing a quiet moment, hinting that they might start a romance now that the truth is out.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old-school detective stories and Japanese history.
